plan.title: Sam asks which book to start with (page example)

transcript.text: hey! so I signed up for ZOH, I'm Sam. I want to start reading again daily, haven't really read a book in like two years lol. Ready when you are!

Hey Sam, I'm ZOH! I'll help you get better at one thing, reading again, with one small step a day. Text "stop" anytime, and tell me whenever you want me to coach differently, like "chill out" or "push me harder."

Two years off is an easy thing to fix. What topics or kinds of books are you into, or is there one you've been meaning to read?
I'm not really sure what I'm into anymore tbh lol. Used to read a lot of thrillers and some sci-fi back in college, then life got busy and I just stopped. What's the best book to start with?

Thrillers and sci-fi is plenty to work with, Sam. We'll pick a fast-paced one together when we build your plan, so you get hooked quickly. When in your day could you realistically read, like 7:30 pm or right before bed?
Evenings for sure, I'm usually free after 9. I can do like 20 to 30 min. Still not sure what the best book to start with is though lol. Is it going to be something I can actually finish?

Yes, you can finish it. 20 to 30 minutes a night is enough to get through a fast thriller in a couple of weeks, and I'll pick one that hooks you early. Where do you want this to get you, like finishing one book or having reading be a nightly habit again?

Honestly both lol. I'd love to finish one and then just have it be a normal nightly thing again like it was in college. Also still wondering what book you'd pick for me, is there a specific one you'd recommend?

Two years off and you still remember thrillers and sci-fi, so my pick is The Martian by Andy Weir. It's a survival thriller with sci-fi at its core, the chapters are short, and it hooks fast.

• Destination: finish The Martian, then keep nightly reading going like in college
• Setup for today: grab a copy (ebook, library or paperback) before 9:30 pm
• Day 1, tonight at 9:30 pm: read from page 1 for 25 minutes, wherever you're comfiest
• Usual schedule: every day, 9:30 pm, 20 to 30 min
• Proof: a photo of the page you stopped on, next to the book or your e-reader. If that's a hassle, a 20-second voice note on what happened so far works too
• Why: a photo keeps it honest, and short chapters mean you can always stop at a natural spot

Each night's read shapes the next one, always aimed at finishing the book. I'll still reach you at 9:30 pm.

What do you think?

grade.summary: ZOH covered the onboarding inputs efficiently in four texts and gave a clear, specific plan with a fitting book pick, proof and a timed first step. The main weak spots are the plan text running close to the length limit and the energy sitting calmer than the pushy default.
